inspection_summary: Inspected all 716 normalized lines. The source develops a speculative but internally explicit chain from gauging CPT, through a quantum phase-space boundary identification compatible with conjugate light-cone variables, to parity-resolved spectral conditions involving Riemann zeta and Dirichlet beta zeros. Its most reusable material is the contrast between classical point identification and quantum canonical identification, the D4/central-diamond construction, the separation of even and odd scattering sectors, and the fact that the proposed boundary discretizes dilation energy while leaving light-cone momentum continuous. Several displayed equations are text-layer fragmented and the two phase-space figures are not recoverable as images, so formula-sensitive units require comparison with the retained PDF. The article proposes a spectral model and physical interpretation; it does not establish the Riemann hypothesis and explicitly leaves absorption-versus-emission, density-of-states, completeness of black-hole microstates, and the unbounded-below spectrum unresolved.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents two phase-space normalizations with the same scattering matrix, changes between light-cone and partial-wave representations, and identifies the commutator and uncertainty scale in the black-hole interpretation.

sections_inspected.label: Dilation symmetries and eigenfunctions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates dilation time evolution, SL(2,R) generators, conformal weight, parity-split energy eigenfunctions, and discrete inversion symmetry.

sections_inspected.label: Global CPT identification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the classical spacetime identification and isolates its failure as a quantum wavefunction condition because U and V are conjugate.

sections_inspected.label: Local phase-space identification and D4 geometry
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs uncertainty-compatible canonical transformations, the finite dihedral action on a central phase-space diamond, and the central involution used as the local CPT boundary identification.

sections_inspected.label: Scattering relations and spectral quantization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the Fourier scattering map, parity-sector gamma factors, CPT action, and functional equations to state zeta/beta zero conditions and interpret nontrivial and trivial spectral points.

sections_inspected.label: Light-cone momentum operators

accepted_units.title: Gauged CPT as an effective low-energy boundary condition
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns a general no-global-symmetries expectation into a concrete modeling move: microscopic gauging may survive semiclassically as a boundary condition rather than as a new visible degree of freedom.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly adopted as a postulate motivated by analogies, not derived from a microscopic quantum-gravity theory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; depends on the physical distinction between ultraviolet gauge symmetry and infrared effective CPT, not on a displayed formula.

accepted_units.title: Hilbert-Polya ambiguity reframed as a boundary-condition problem
accepted_units.why_material: The passage cleanly separates three missing ingredients in spectral approaches to zeta zeros—the self-adjoint operator, its function space/boundary condition, and the physical origin of that choice—then identifies gauged CPT as the proposed source of discretization.
accepted_units.context_note: The zeta/beta spectrum and black-hole-chaos connection are announced here and argued later; this span is a problem statement and roadmap, not evidence for the announced result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded, with named dependence on the dilation operator, Hilbert-Polya conjecture, and random-matrix spectral statistics.

accepted_units.title: Two phase-space normalizations with one scattering matrix
accepted_units.why_material: The source exhibits two Hamiltonian descriptions—one with partial-wave-dependent commutators and one with a common phase-space cell plus an l-dependent shift—that are asserted to yield the same scattering matrix. This separates representation choices from the scattering observable.
accepted_units.context_note: The equality of scattering matrices is attributed to earlier work rather than rederived in this span; the partial-wave expansion supplies the local representation context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (1)-(3) are essential. Their sums, commutators, and l-dependent factors are legible but should be scan-verified before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Black-hole coordinates turn the dilation algebra into near-horizon scattering data
accepted_units.why_material: The passage maps the abstract Hamiltonians to Schwarzschild partial waves, relates Kruskal and asymptotic-observer coordinates, and interprets the U-V commutator as both a gravitational back-reaction effect and a minimal phase-space/causal-diamond uncertainty.
accepted_units.context_note: The identification with the shockwave scattering matrix is cited from prior work. The unit supplies the physical dictionary needed for the later CPT boundary condition, not an independent derivation of black-hole dynamics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted metric, coordinate map (5), energy-unit conversion, and commutator. The metric extraction at lines 177-187 is formula-sensitive and requires PDF verification for exact use.

accepted_units.title: Dilation dynamics decomposes into SL(2,R) weight and parity sectors
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies Hamiltonian evolution with dilation, places the generators in an SL(2,R) algebra, converts energy into conformal weight, and resolves the twofold degeneracy into even and odd eigenfunction branches. This parity split later determines which L-function enters the quantization condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The classical exponential separation is presented as a chaos property, while the quantum statements concern eigenfunctions and representation theory; these signals should not be conflated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (6) and the displayed generators/eigenfunctions are central. Superscripts and exponents are text-layer-fragmented, so exact normalizations need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Discrete conformal inversions act automorphically on energy eigenfunctions
accepted_units.why_material: The inversion V maps to plus or minus 1/V is lifted to a weighted action on functions, under which the parity eigenfunctions have fixed eigenvalues. This supplies the symmetry template for the later canonical phase-space maps.
accepted_units.context_note: The source calls the eigenfunctions quasi-automorphic with respect to the generated discrete subgroup; no broader automorphic classification is established here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation (7), the conformal weight from the preceding unit, and parity signs; the weighted inversion formula should be checked against the PDF before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Classical global CPT identification cannot be imposed on quantum conjugate coordinates
accepted_units.why_material: After deriving the partial-wave CPT identification and its antipodal classical consequence, the source pinpoints the obstruction: a pointwise condition on both U and V is not a valid wavefunction condition when those variables are canonically conjugate.
accepted_units.context_note: The projection of even-l modes and single-exterior interpretation belong to the classical spacetime proposal; the quantum construction that replaces it begins later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses spherical-harmonic conjugation/parity formulas and equation (8). The conceptual obstruction is recoverable from prose even if phase conventions need checking.

accepted_units.title: Uncertainty forces CPT identification from spacetime points to phase-space states
accepted_units.why_material: This passage reframes a geometric identification as a quantum phase-space condition and states that it must constrain both ingoing and outgoing wavefunctions because they use conjugate representations. It is the key bridge from the classical obstruction to the canonical construction.
accepted_units.context_note: The elementary-cell and constant-energy statements motivate the construction; the actual maps and spectral consequences follow in subsequent units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual content is prose-grounded but uses the U-V phase plane, the uncertainty relation from equation (6), and the inversion symmetry from equation (7).

accepted_units.title: Canonical inversion extensions generate a D4 central phase-space diamond
accepted_units.why_material: The source enlarges coordinate inversion into area-preserving transformations of conjugate variables, observes their Hamiltonian action, and shows that at fixed UV they generate an eight-element dihedral action on four phase-space cells. This replaces an inadmissible point identification with a finite canonical symmetry structure.
accepted_units.context_note: The group and geometry claims are made for fixed UV=h. The associated figure is not contained in this unit and the normalized text does not preserve its geometry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (9)-(10), Jacobian signs, and the D4 action are essential. Fraction layout and plus/minus labels are extraction-sensitive and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A central involution induces the local CPT boundary on UV hyperbolae
accepted_units.why_material: The central element T2+ is chosen as the light-cone CPT identification; edge identification gives an RP2 topology, and commutation with dilation transports the condition from the central diamond to every paired point on UV=plus or minus h. The homotopy note explains the resulting two path classes.
accepted_units.context_note: The topology statement is supported by a cited external explanation, while this source uses it operationally to define the wavefunction boundary condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exact T2+ convention from equation (10), the central-diamond geometry, and formula typography for UV=plus or minus h; scan verification is needed for exact signs.

accepted_units.title: Fourier scattering separates even and odd dilation channels
accepted_units.why_material: The in/out partial-wave expansion and Fourier transform convert near-horizon scattering into coefficient relations with distinct gamma-function factors for even and odd eigenfunctions. This is the analytic bridge between phase-space symmetry and the two later L-function conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: The scattering transform is attributed to gravitational back-reaction, and this span derives channel relations only; the CPT boundary has not yet been combined with them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (11)-(13) are indispensable and heavily layout-sensitive in extraction, especially gamma arguments, powers, and hbar factors; exact formulas require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Quantum CPT acts on in/out wavefunctions along Planckian hyperbolae
accepted_units.why_material: The source combines the canonical map with conjugation and spherical parity to formulate CPT directly on both scattering representations, then restricts the identification to the dilation orbit |UV|=h. This is the quantum replacement for the rejected global pointwise condition.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 424-436 are a figure and caption showing the proposed geometry; only labels and caption survive extraction. The prose at 449-452 supplies the recoverable conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (14)-(15) are fragmented across lines and Figure 2 is image-dependent. The action, signs, arguments, and geometry must be scan-verified before formal reuse.

accepted_units.title: Even-sector boundary plus zeta functional equation yields a zero condition
accepted_units.why_material: Combining the even scattering relation, CPT identification, and zeta functional equation produces an equivalence relation asserted to hold over the full one-parameter locus |UV|=h; the source argues nonzero eigenfunctions then require paired zeta zeros, with real energy placing s on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a quantization condition inside the proposed model, not a proof that all nontrivial zeta zeros lie on the critical line or that the operator satisfies the full Hilbert-Polya program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The functional equation and equation (16) are essential, but equation (16) is substantially fragmented by extraction. Exact iff conditions, conjugations, coefficients, and powers require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Odd parity changes the spectral condition from zeta to Dirichlet beta
accepted_units.why_material: The sign carried by odd eigenfunctions modifies the equivalence relation, and the Dirichlet beta functional equation supplies the corresponding discrete odd-wave spectrum. This exposes how a representation-theoretic branch choice changes the arithmetic spectral object.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit is explicitly parallel to the even-sector construction and should be compared, not treated as an independent operator derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (17) and the beta functional equation are text-layer-fragmented; signs, gamma arguments, powers, and coefficient conjugations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The boundary condition regularizes dilation while breaking parity degeneracy
accepted_units.why_material: The source interprets the local phase-space boundary as a symmetry-respecting alternative to a naive cutoff, decomposes the complete shifted Hamiltonian into partial-wave contributions, and explains that zeta/beta branches break the original even/odd degeneracy while retaining m-degeneracy.
accepted_units.context_note: The solar-mass density estimate is an illustrative physical scale, not validation of the spectral construction; the Hamiltonian decomposition depends on the earlier choice of normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The spectral sum and numerical scale are formula-sensitive. The prose-level claims about regularization, degeneracy, and density are recoverable, but exact factors need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Trivial zeros are mapped to imaginary-energy resonances
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes nontrivial real-energy spectral conditions from trivial zeros and interprets the latter through poles and zeros of the scattering matrix on imaginary energy axes as unstable resonances.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an interpretation within the stated scattering model; it does not independently establish a resonance theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted trivial-zero formulas and analytic continuation of equations (11)-(13); exact sign and parity indexing require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The same identification leaves light-cone momentum spectra continuous
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the boundary map to Kruskal momentum eigenfunctions constrains coefficients but does not discretize momentum. This is a valuable counterpoint: the boundary condition is observable-selective rather than a universal discretizer, and the source reads that invariance as evidence for horizon smoothness.
accepted_units.context_note: The smooth-horizon statement is explicitly only a first indication. The exact coefficient relation is less secure than the prose conclusion because of extraction damage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses plane-wave eigenfunctions and a fragmented T2+ coefficient relation. Exact phases and arguments require PDF checking; the conclusion that continuity is unaffected is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: The same zero relations may encode missing spectral lines rather than emitted levels
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion records a materially different Connes-style interpretation: equations (16)-(17) could describe absorption gaps in a continuum rather than a discrete emission spectrum, and deciding among absorption, emission, or both requires comparison of trace formulas with zeta density of states.
accepted_units.context_note: No such comparison is performed in this source, so the alternatives remain unresolved and prevent treating the physical spectral dictionary as settled.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded but refers back to the formula-sensitive equivalence relations (16)-(17) and to external trace-formula work.

accepted_units.title: Entropy, multiparticle observables, and the missing ground state remain open tests
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies concrete ways the proposal could fail or be sharpened: a density/partition-function calculation must test black-hole entropy and state completeness, multiparticle observables remain unchecked, and the discrete spectrum is still unbounded below despite gauging CPT.
accepted_units.context_note: The opening richness claim summarizes earlier results; the reusable content is the explicit set of unresolved predictions and the admission that the boundary condition may be insufficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose-grounded; the entropy and spectral-ground-state tests depend on the model's earlier energy interpretation but not on a new displayed formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From gauged symmetry to arithmetic spectral condition
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Within the proposed model, gauging CPT is operationalized as a canonical phase-space boundary condition; after parity-resolved scattering, functional equations convert that condition into zeta and beta zero constraints.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis is source-conditional, formula-sensitive, and neither derives the ultraviolet gauging premise nor proves the Riemann hypothesis.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Representation choice versus observable consequence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Equivalent Hamiltonian normalizations can preserve the scattering matrix while the added boundary condition affects observables selectively: dilation energy becomes discrete in the proposal, whereas light-cone momentum remains continuous.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equivalences and observable behavior are established only for the cited near-horizon construction, not as a general principle for arbitrary Hamiltonians or boundaries.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parity as a selector of arithmetic spectrum
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reflection parity propagates through inversion eigenvalues and scattering gamma factors so that the even branch is paired with Riemann zeta and the odd branch with Dirichlet beta, breaking their initial twofold degeneracy.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact branch correspondence relies on extracted signs, powers, and gamma factors that require verification against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A spectral dictionary constrained by its failure modes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source offers a layered dictionary—nontrivial zeros as real-energy levels, trivial zeros as imaginary-energy resonances, and possibly zeros as missing continuum lines—while naming density, entropy, multiparticle, and ground-state tests that could distinguish or invalidate these readings.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These are competing physical interpretations, not mutually verified consequences, and the proposed discriminating calculations are not carried out here.

within_source_saturation: All usable mathematical prose from lines 1-716 is accounted for. The accepted units cover each nonrepetitive mechanism, representation change, obstruction, spectral condition, comparison, and explicit limitation. Further units would predominantly duplicate the abstract/conclusion, isolate routine formula manipulation from its governing mechanism, select bibliography/administrative matter, or pretend to recover the two degraded figures and fragmented formulas without the retained PDF.
stop_reason: Source-specific saturation was reached after the full 716-line inspection: the body’s complete chain from the CPT postulate through canonical phase-space identification and parity-resolved zeta/beta conditions is represented, together with the continuous-momentum counterexample and every stated interpretive limitation; the remaining material is repeated summary, page furniture, acknowledgements, references, or extraction-defective graphical/formula detail.
